topic: What happens if you drink only cold water?
title: What Happens If You Drink Only Cold Water?
sources: Boschmann M, Steiniger J, Hille U, et al. 'Water-induced thermogenesis.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2003;88(12):6015-9 (PMID 14671205): drinking 500 ml of water raised resting metabolic rate by about 30% for roughly an hour

Brown CM, Dulloo AG, Montani JP. 'Water-induced thermogenesis reconsidered: the effects of osmolality and water temperature on energy expenditure after drinking.' J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2006;91(9):3598-602 (PMID 16822824): energy expenditure after drinking rises MORE when the water is cold (3 C vs 37 C)

Physics of warming: heating 500 g of ice-cold water (about 4 C) to body temperature (37 C) costs about 33 x 500 = 16.5 kcal (specific heat of water 1 kcal/kg/C); that is roughly one bite of bread (~15-25 kcal per slice of white bread, ~70-80 kcal per slice) — phrased conservatively as 'a bite of food'

Charrière N, Miles-Chan JL, Montani JP, Dulloo AG. 'Water-induced thermogenesis and fat oxidation: a reassessment.' Nutr Diabetes 2015;5(12):e190 (PMID 26690288): effect size varies between individuals; keep claims conservative

lines.text: What happens if you only drink cold water?
lines.caps: What *happens | if you only | drink *cold water?

lines.text: Every glass makes your body work.
Ice-cold water arrives near zero degrees.
Your body has to warm it to thirty-seven.
That big glass costs about sixteen calories.
And cold water revs your metabolism even harder.
Sound like a free diet hack?
Sixteen calories is one bite of food.
Your body already burns thousands a day.
So cold water won't hurt you.
But it won't change your body either.
